messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: Elevated 5xx rate (502/504) from private inference gateway in prod-vpc-us-west-2, multiple customers reporting errors, trending up over last 7m. Pager: maya.

maya (oncall): I'm up, looking. Which gateway exactly?

chris (infra-sre): seeing same in metrics dashboard — 504s spiking from gw-infer-azb (private) starting ~10:35 UTC. Error traces show backend connection resets to model host pool.

sam (netops): I pulled VPC flow logs, lots of short-lived TCP attempts out to external model registry IPs coming from the NAT instance in az-b. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT.

maya (oncall): quick checks: curl from a debug pod to model endpoint returns 504.

maya (oncall): ```bash
kubectl run -i --rm debug --image=curlimages/curl --restart=Never -- curl -v https://10.200.34.12:8080/ping
* Connected to 10.200.34.12 (10.200.34.12) port 8080 (#0)
* Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
* Empty reply from server
* HTTP return code said to be 0
```

chris (infra-sre): interesting — on the NAT host the conntrack table looks huge. ssh'ed to nat-host-azb: `sudo conntrack -S` shows high COUNTERS, and `ss -s` shows many TIME_WAIT.

maya (oncall): can you paste exact counts?

chris (infra-sre): ```
# sudo conntrack -S
cpu=0 found=436789 invalid=0 ignore=0 delete=420000
entries=176000 menmem=...
# ss -s | grep -E \"TIME_WAIT|estab\"
TIME-WAIT: 51234
ESTAB: 1200
```

sam (netops): that TIME_WAIT is huge for a NAT instance-sized EIP pool. Looks like we hit ephemeral port exhaustion — OS ephemeral range + number of NAT EIPs can't sustain the burst. I've seen this when a routing change increases fanout.

maya (oncall): did we roll any peering or route changes recently?

deploy-bot: deploy-redwood-inference: accepted roll: route-update-azb -> completed 10:27 UTC :rocket:

sam (netops): aha — route-update-azb pushed a static route prepending to prefer a new transit path through a partner appliance. That doubled egress path for some subnets, effectively doubling simultaneous flows through nat-host-azb.

chris (infra-sre): root cause hypothesis: route change increased flows through single NAT instance (az-b), causing ephemeral port pool to exhaust -> upstream connections drop/timeout -> 502/504 at inference gateway.

jen (customer-success): customers A and C reported errors in their integration tests ~10:35 and are now seeing timeouts in production. They're asking for ETA and mitigation.

maya (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) add a hot secondary NAT gateway (az-c) and shift a subset of subnet egress to it 2) enable temporary hosted fallback for impacted customers 3) increase ephemeral port range on nat-hosts as intermediate measure 4) rollback route-update-azb if necessary. Which one is fastest?

sam (netops): quickest: provision secondary NAT (already available but needs route target updates). I can add a route for a small CIDR range to prefer nat-azc. Will do a small shift (10%) and measure.

chris (infra-sre): I'll run conntrack cleanup and bump net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range on nat-host-azb to widen ephemeral range while we re-route. Command I plan: ```bash
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='15000 61000'
sudo conntrack -F && sleep 3 && systemctl restart nat-proxy
```

maya (oncall): go for it. sam, ping me when the route change is in place. I'll notify customers with a short update.

sam (netops): Route ripples done for 10% of the subnets to nat-azc (manual change). Monitoring...

sam (netops): initial metrics: 5xx rate down ~30% on shifted traffic, overall 5xx still elevated but trending down.

chris (infra-sre): conntrack cleared and ephemeral range widened on nat-host-azb. TIME_WAIT dropped to ~12k. ESTAB still ~1k.

maya (oncall): great. customers reporting fewer errors. jen can you update the CS thread?

jen (customer-success): pinged customers with: "We're mitigating — rerouting traffic and expanding NAT capacity; you may see intermittent successful requests while we finish. ETA 20-30m."

maya (oncall): next steps: continue incremental re-route to secondary NAT until load drops below threshold, watch model host error traces for resets. If we don't see improvement in 30m, rollback route-update-azb.

chris (infra-sre): filing follow-up action: we should auto-scale NAT capacity or use multiple EIPs/EIPs-per-NAT to avoid single-point port exhaustion in high-fanout deploys. I'll create a ticket after this.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=P2, start=1768501234, impacted=private-inference-gateway, mitigation=in-flight (nat re-route, conntrack flush, ephemeral-range bump).

maya (oncall): marking on-call handoff for next shift in case this persists. If anyone sees recurrence after full re-route, escalate to sev1.

sam (netops): continuing to move remaining subnets now (additional 40%). Will report back in 10m. :thumbsup:

chris (infra-sre): logs show backend connection resets decreasing. Good signal.

maya (oncall): thanks team — keeping thread open until fully stable and CS confirms customers recovered.

(10m later)
sam (netops): all targeted subnets moved to nat-azc. 5xx now ~8% of baseline, down from 60% spike.

jen (customer-success): customers A and C confirmed they're green. One asked for root cause write-up.

chris (infra-sre): creating post-incident doc with timeline, root cause (ephemeral port exhaustion caused by route-change-induced fanout to single NAT), mitigations applied, and follow-ups (autoscale NAT / multi-EIP deployment / preflight route rollout checks).

maya (oncall): closing live mitigation. Will hand off to chris for postmortem and follow-ups. Thanks all. :tada:
